source.title: JASMINE: Arabic GPT Models for Few-Shot Learning
source.authors: E. Nagoudi; M. Abdul-Mageed; AbdelRahim Elmadany; Alcides Alcoba Inciarte; Md. Tawkat Islam Khondaker

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some tables and Arabic text are affected by extraction/encoding artifacts, but Table 3's perplexity values are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out perplexity for Arabic models at four parameter sizes, extending the parameter-scaling question to Arabic. It does not fit or test a scaling law.
record.gate_note: Table 3 reports zero-shot BPE-token-level perplexity for four JASMINE sizes on six held-out datasets; these are the relevant size-sweep results. The study also reports downstream benchmark results, but does not fit or evaluate predictions of downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss. Other benchmark and generation results do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Table 3 gives held-out perplexity for four JASMINE sizes (350M–6.7B) on six Arabic test sets. This bears weakly on V1 in a new language setting. It is a model-release paper: no power-law fit, exponents, token or compute sweep, and only about 1.3 orders of magnitude in parameters.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly wrong. The authors do not discuss perplexity trends with size. They conclude that JASMINE clearly outperforms AraGPT2 and mGPT baselines on perplexity (6.7B average PPL 42.25) and excels in few-shot learning and fluent generation. No scaling-law conclusion is drawn.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains Arabic GPT-style models and evaluates held-out perplexity across four sizes; it does not use the original studies' scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Perplexity levels vary substantially by evaluation dataset; all six show decreasing values across the four JASMINE sizes.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The reported metric is perplexity rather than cross-entropy loss. Only four sizes are tested, over 350M–6.7B parameters, and no power-law fit, exponent, uncertainty, or evaluation across several orders of magnitude is reported. Individual token counts and compute budgets for the model runs are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were retained. The paper's downstream benchmark scores are not rows for the tested scaling-law version because they are not used to test or predict downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss.

untested.parts: Power-law form or exponent; token and compute scaling; several orders of magnitude (only 350M–6.7B); whether data was a bottleneck (all sizes trained 500k steps, batch/tokens not stated).
All; no extrapolation from small fits.
All; no shape comparison at fixed size.
All; poetry and tweet further-pretraining reports no loss scaling.
Predictability from scale or loss not analysed; downstream scores across sizes are reported but not fitted.

missing.what: Downstream few-shot scores across JASMINE sizes; mostly increasing with size but non-monotone in places. Relevant only if V6 is read loosely; no predictability analysis.
All four models trained for the same 500k steps; batch size and token counts are not stated. This bears on whether data was a bottleneck for the V1 size sweep.

record.verdict_notes: Log of perplexity (mean token cross-entropy) for AraWiki: 3.95, 3.58, 3.50, 3.41 across 350M, 1.3B, 2.7B, 6.7B. The log-log slope drops from about -0.17 to about -0.03 after 1.3B. Evidence is weak: four points, no uncertainty, and the step count is held fixed. Model sizes are confounded with depth and width changes (Table 2).

versions.untested_parts: Reports perplexity across parameter sizes, but does not fit a power law, report exponents, measure cross-entropy directly, vary training tokens or compute, or cover several orders of magnitude.
No small-run fits or predictions for larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Additional poetry and tweet training is reported, but the study does not test whether power-law forms hold in those regimes or modalities.
The paper evaluates downstream tasks at different model sizes, but does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, or curve departures.

relationships.condition: JASMINE Arabic GPT-Neo models, 350M–6.7B, fixed 500k steps, six held-out Arabic sets (BPE-token perplexity)
relationships.reason: Perplexity falls monotonically on all six sets (r2, r6, r10, r14, r18, r22 large drops). Gains beyond 1.3B are much smaller (r3–r24 partial), so the curve bends well away from a single power law. With equal training steps, a data bottleneck may explain this; no fit is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Perplexity decreased on all six sets, with much smaller gains beyond 1.3B parameters and no reported power-law fit.

source_check.reason: All listed values decrease with size. Smaller absolute perplexity gains do not establish departure from a power law in loss, which is log perplexity. No fit, several-orders-of-magnitude sweep, or verified non-bottleneck conditions establish a limitation of V1; these unresolved requirements cannot justify limits_scope.

labels.reason: All listed values decrease with size. Smaller absolute perplexity gains do not establish departure from a power law in loss, which is log perplexity. relation.reason: The study's own size-dependent held-out perplexity results bear on V1, although they cannot resolve the full claim.

tranche.reason: Held-out perplexity across four model sizes provides weak evidence relevant to V1 in an Arabic setting, without establishing its functional form.

source_check.notes: Table 1 reports corpus token counts, but per-model training token budgets are unstated. Adjacent-size values suggested in the verdict fixes are available comparisons, not explicitly designated scaling baselines.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: JASMINE models on the six Table 3 held-out datasets, from 350M to 6.7B parameters
reader_labels.reason: Perplexity decreases with each increase in model size (r1–r24), consistent with a size-related decline, but the study does not fit a power law or establish its form or range.
